answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. It survives because finality only counts for established attestators, so a fresh cluster cannot push transactions until it proves honesty across many epochs. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a relic as the anchor of the cost.
